title: Making vegetables more appealing
titleChinese: 让蔬菜看起来更加美味诱人
paragraphs: As a child, I was always told to 'eat my greens'. These were the unappealing vegetables that sat on the edge of my plate. Peas, broccoli and green beans, all looked and tasted disgusting. Let's face it, when there were so many other edible treats to enjoy, why eat boring veg?

Since then my taste buds have developed and I'm also fully aware of the health benefits of eating fresh vegetables. But we still need reminding of the amazing goodness these green superfoods give us. In the UK, a campaign based on advice from the World Health Organization has been running for several years to encourage us to eat our '5 A Day' - five portions of fruit and vegetables. That's because evidence has shown there are significant health benefits to getting at least five 80g portions of a variety of fruit and vegetables every day.

But I struggle trying to fit these five portions into my daily diet, partly because I have a sweet tooth and vegetables are, well, tasteless. Researchers have been looking at how to make eating vegetables more attractive. They analysed the psychology behind our food choices and found that most of us are motivated by taste. Brad Turnwald from Stanford University says that "studies show that people tend to think of healthier options as less tasty for some reason."

His team carried out an experiment in the university cafeteria where they gave vegetables seductive names and found sales increased by 25 per cent. They got rid of healthy labels such as 'wholesome' and gave identical dishes names like 'sizzlin' beans', 'dynamite beets' and 'twisted citrus-glazed carrots'. It seems that these indulgent names tempted diners to fill their plates. Brad Turnwald says that "labels really can influence our sensory experience, affecting how tasty and filling we think food will be."

In Europe, a project called VeggieEAT has also been trying to find ways to get people to eat more veg. Project leader, Professor Heather Hartwell believes in "health by stealth", subtly nudging people into eating the right things. One idea has been to put a picture of a tasty looking fruit on a supermarket trolley as a hint about buying something from the fruit aisle. She says, "Choice is a really complex thing. But this study suggests that giving vegetables an indulgent tag can help raise their hierarchy."
Certainly, eating 'twisted citrus-glazed carrots' does sound tempting, even if it just tastes like a carrot, but if it makes us eat more vegetables then that can only be a good thing for our health.

vocabulary.entry: unappealing [adj.] /ˌʌnəˈpiːlɪŋ/ 无吸引力的；不吸引人的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The room was painted in an unappealing shade of green.
vocabulary.translation: 房间刷了一种不吸引人的绿色调。

vocabulary.entry: disgusting [adj.] /dɪsˈɡʌstɪŋ/ 令人厌恶的；令人作呕的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The smell from the bin was absolutely disgusting.
vocabulary.translation: 垃圾桶里散发出的气味令人作呕。

vocabulary.entry: edible [adj.] /ˈedəbəl/ 可食用的
vocabulary.example: These berries are edible, but those are poisonous.
vocabulary.translation: 这些浆果是可食用的，但那些是有毒的。

vocabulary.entry: goodness [n.] /ˈɡʊdnəs/ 营养成分；精华 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Whole foods are full of natural goodness.
vocabulary.translation: 天然食品富含营养成分。

vocabulary.entry: sweet tooth [n.] /ˌswiːt ˈtuːθ/ 喜欢吃甜食 (口语)
vocabulary.example: I have a sweet tooth and can't resist chocolate.
vocabulary.translation: 我喜欢吃甜食，无法抗拒巧克力。

vocabulary.entry: seductive [adj.] /sɪˈdʌktɪv/ 诱人的；有吸引力的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The dessert menu was very seductive.
vocabulary.translation: 甜点菜单非常诱人。

vocabulary.entry: indulgent [adj.] /ɪnˈdʌldʒənt/ 纵容的；诱人的 (此处指食物诱人)
vocabulary.example: The rich chocolate cake was an indulgent treat.
vocabulary.translation: 浓郁的巧克力蛋糕是一种诱人的美食。

vocabulary.entry: subtly [adv.] /ˈsʌtli/ 巧妙地；微妙地
vocabulary.example: The ad subtly encourages people to buy more.
vocabulary.translation: 这则广告巧妙地鼓励人们购买更多。

vocabulary.entry: hierarchy [n.] /ˈhaɪərɑːki/ 等级制度；层级
vocabulary.example: In the world of fashion, some brands sit at the top of the hierarchy.
vocabulary.translation: 在时尚界，一些品牌处于等级体系的顶端。

vocabulary.entry: tempting [adj.] /ˈtemptɪŋ/ 诱人的；有吸引力的
vocabulary.example: The offer of a free holiday was very tempting.
vocabulary.translation: 免费度假的提议非常诱人。

vocabulary.entry: taste bud [n.] /ˈteɪst bʌd/ 味蕾 (解剖学词汇)
vocabulary.example: Spicy food can stimulate your taste buds.
vocabulary.translation: 辛辣食物可以刺激你的味蕾。

vocabulary.entry: superfood [n.] /ˈsuːpəfuːd/ 超级食物 (口语；专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Kale is often described as a superfood.
vocabulary.translation: 羽衣甘蓝常被描述为一种超级食物。

vocabulary.entry: campaign [n.] /kæmˈpeɪn/ 运动；活动
vocabulary.example: The advertising campaign was very successful.
vocabulary.translation: 这场广告宣传活动非常成功。

vocabulary.entry: portion [n.] /ˈpɔːʃən/ 一份食物
vocabulary.example: A portion of chips is not very healthy.
vocabulary.translation: 一份薯条不太健康。

vocabulary.entry: psychology [n.] /saɪˈkɒlədʒi/ 心理学
vocabulary.example: Consumer psychology affects how people shop.
vocabulary.translation: 消费者心理影响人们的购物方式。

vocabulary.entry: cafeteria [n.] /ˌkæfəˈtɪəriə/ 自助餐厅；食堂
vocabulary.example: The school cafeteria serves lunch to students.
vocabulary.translation: 学校食堂为学生提供午餐。

vocabulary.entry: wholesome [adj.] /ˈhəʊlsəm/ 有益健康的；有营养的
vocabulary.example: Wholesome meals are made from fresh ingredients.
vocabulary.translation: 有益健康的餐食由新鲜食材制成。

vocabulary.entry: sensory [adj.] /ˈsensəri/ 感觉的；感官的
vocabulary.example: The sensory experience of eating involves taste, smell, and texture.
vocabulary.translation: 进食的感官体验包括味道、气味和质地。

vocabulary.entry: nudge [v.] /nʌdʒ/ 轻推；引导 (比喻)
vocabulary.example: The government is nudging people towards healthier choices.
vocabulary.translation: 政府正在引导人们做出更健康的选择。

vocabulary.entry: aisle [n.] /aɪl/ 过道；通道
vocabulary.example: You can find pasta in the third aisle.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以在第三个过道找到意大利面。
